_meta.change: split the cogPG.PG113 whole-volume CGPG dump into per-work corpus files
_meta.plan_basis: read at the row. The two Constantine works sit inside one contiguous run of loci, so their internal boundary is taken at the display heads rather than at a gap.
_meta.shared_row_rule: a served row holding a work boundary is assigned to exactly one work, normally the one whose incipit the row carries; the plan records the decision as the ranges themselves
_meta.reversible: To revert: for every carved work file listed under 'works', drop its rows whose locus starts 'PG113.' (delete the file when it was 'created'), strip the 'PG113.' prefix from their loci, re-insert them and the archived 'dropped_duplicates' rows into data/corpus/cogPG.PG113.jsonl together with the residual rows, sorted by locus, and restore data/cgpg_works.json, data/tlg_crosswalk.json/.tsv, and data/corrections_log/provenance.json from the parent commit (or simply git revert the commit; old sha256 below verifies). Every moved row's text is byte-identical; only urn and locus changed.

works.title: De thematibus
works.secondary_reason: work is served from byzantium.gr's manual transcription, which beats OCR of the same text per the source-precedence tie-break (the precedent is scylitzes-continuatus.continuatio-scylitzae, filed the same way); this Migne witness is kept, not served

incipit_checks.incipit: Περὶ τῶν θεμάτων τῶν ἀνηκόντων τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν Ῥωμαίων

works.evidence: Locus 39 is the work's own title line. 81 is the last page before the Synecdemus head at 82. 10,402 tokens against 9,330 served, a ratio of 1.11.

works.title: De administrando imperio
works.secondary_reason: work is served from byzantium.gr's manual transcription, which beats OCR of the same text per the source-precedence tie-break (the precedent is scylitzes-continuatus.continuatio-scylitzae, filed the same way); this Migne witness is kept, not served
works.evidence: Locus 90 carries the proem head and its opening, Υἱὸς σοφὸς εὐφραίνει πατέρα, which is how De administrando imperio begins. 223 opens a different Constantinian compilation head. 39,340 tokens against 39,545 served, a ratio of 0.99.

residual.note: 82-89 is Hierocles' Synecdemus, printed between the two Constantine works; 223-313 opens on a further Constantinian compilation head; 318-323 are Dexippus testimonia; 328-489 is the Excerpta de legationibus, whose text is already held under the individual historians and whose disposition is a call this carve does not make. None of these is carved here.

corrections_mirror_note: data/corrections_log/applied.jsonl keys this volume's corrections by bare column locus under cogPG.PG113; per the rekey_corrections_log.py convention for cogPG.* bare-locus rows they are left unchanged (historical). The locus map above makes the linkage reconstructable.
source: CGPG per-work carve of PG113, plan data/cgpg_carve_plan.json

superseded.why: carve_cgpg_volume.py fell back to the carve plan's _meta.date when the volume entry had none, which no entry did, so this record was stamped with the date the plan file was written rather than the date the carve ran. The real date is the commit that first added this audit.
